data.long_meaning: From the Greek word 'techne' meaning art, skill, or craft. In Christianity, Arte represents the divine gift of creativity and expression. The name Arte carries the meaning “Art, Skill, Craft” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Arte usually hope their child will grow to embody art, skill, craft and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_latin.name: Arte
in_latin.long_meaning: Arte, nomine feminino, est genus Latinum, quod originem habet a vocabulo 'Arte', quod significat 'rex', 'regina', 'dominus'. In lingua Latina antiqua, 'Arte' erat nomen feminarum, quae significabant 'reginam', 'dominam', 'potentem'. In religione Christiana, 'Arte' est nomen feminarum, quae significabant 'Christi Servam', 'Servam Christi', 'Christi Fidem'.

in_english.name: Arte
in_english.meaning: Queen, King, Ruler, Lord, Mistress, Sovereign
in_english.long_meaning: Arte is a name of Hebrew origin, meaning 'queen' or 'ruler'. The name Arte has its roots in the Hebrew words 'Artah' and 'Artahim', which signify 'queen' or 'ruler'. In biblical Hebrew, the name Arte is associated with the concept of royalty and power. In the early Christian church, the name Arte was used to signify 'Christian Queen' or 'Queen of Heaven'. Today, the name Arte is used in various Christian cultures to signify 'ruler' or 'sovereign'. The name Arte is also associated with qualities such as wisdom, strength, and courage.
